bug_semantics: The scanner extracted pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL references but treated a reference as an issue only when its module/name matched a finite deny-list. A malicious pickle could therefore compose pydoc.locate to resolve/import an arbitrary module such as os with operator.methodcaller to invoke a method such as system; because locate and methodcaller were not denied, the scan produced no dangerous issue even though unpickling the same payload could execute a command.
flaw_origin: The initial scanner implementation in src/picklescan/scanner.py introduced a default-allow-by-omission decision: _suspicious_globals listed only selected modules/functions, and scan_pickle_bytes incremented issues_count only for an explicit match. pydoc and operator were absent, so pydoc.locate and operator.methodcaller were unreported from the first implementation. Later commits 108b06040de644c7aeb5f22d8b10dd9c5d282386 (operator.attrgetter) and 93764d62af72b0ec3e2dd693ab6a9774abbed953 (pydoc.pipepager) were incomplete mitigations, not introducers, because the bypass already existed.

reasoning: The vulnerable behavior began when c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e first implemented the scanner: imports outside its finite list did not increment issues_count, so the advisory's pydoc.locate and operator.methodcaller chain was already a clean scan bypass. The direct parent 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326 has no scanner.py, proving absence rather than merely relying on blame. Subsequent attrgetter and pipepager entries partially expanded the deny-list but did not create the underlying omission, and v0.0.32 still has those incomplete entries. Commit 70c1c6c31beb6baaf52c8db1b6c3c0e84a6f9dab directly closes the named path and is the v0.0.33 release target, matching the advisory boundary. Inspection of only the BIC commit object found no AI attribution marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
